Chicago's world-famous skyline tells only half the story. Scattered through downtown are masterpieces by Picasso, Chagall, Miró, and Kapoor, transforming the city into an open-air museum. After the Great Fire of 1871, Chicago rebuilt itself as a global architectural powerhouse, but its public art-often hiding in plain sight-adds color, depth, and character to the “City of Big Shoulders.” Begin at Cloud Gate-Anish Kapoor's gleaming “Bean” that reflects the skyline-and explore works of public art that define Chicago's streets. From towering steel sculptures to vibrant mosaics and surreal installations, discover how some of the 20th century's greatest artists left their mark on the city. Along the way, marvel at The Rookery, a stunning 19th-century skyscraper with a Frank Lloyd Wright-designed lobby, and gaze up at the soaring Willis Tower, once the tallest building in the world. Whether you're drawn to abstract giants or intricate murals, this tour unveils the bold artistic visions that make Chicago's downtown an ever-evolving canvas.

facts.description: Learn about Chicago's Architectural Marvels from an Engineer! As an independent business, we have the flexibility and passion to create tour routes that aren't necessarily what most tourists think to book when visiting Chicago - we leave that to the big-box companies. We have the freedom and drive to create tour experiences according to what we - as knowledgeable experts in Chicago history and architecture - find most fascinating about our city. And truly one of the most fascinating yet least appreciated aspects of any city is its many engineering stories. Chicago is literally the birthplace of the skyscraper: imagine what incredible stories of engineering feats it has to tell! Join Inside Chicago Walking Tours on our newest - and admittedly very-nerdy-but-fun-because-it's-nerdy! - route that dives into the engineering perspective of our world-famous architecture. On this route, you'll cover more than 150 years of engineering evolution, learning from a real engineer (from the best engineering school in the country!), who makes the information accessible and graspable without ever dumbing it down. This is not “engineering for dummies”: it is engineering for all of us, as we believe that everyone can understand and be fascinated by these concepts if taught in an engaging and fun way. You'll see a building from the “father of the skyscraper,” who was actually an engineer and a classmate of Gustav Eiffel (as in, Eiffel Tower!). You'll learn how a building might get a “haunted” reputation simply because it settled unevenly on its “floating” foundation. You'll marvel at the numerous ways Chicago's famous buildings handle forces coming from gravity and wind. You'll learn about one of the greatest engineering feats of the United States, and why and how we accomplished it. And of course, as on all of our tours, you'll visit the interiors of a few buildings to truly get that sense that you've seen inside Chicago! Tour Details - Runs rain or shine!
